fullData.title: Total Apples in Equal Groups
fullData.subject: Arithmetic

problem.statement: Maya has 3 baskets of apples. Each basket contains 4 apples. How many apples does Maya have in total?

fullData.solutionStrategy: Multiply the number of baskets by the number of apples in each basket to find the total.

content.altText: Three groups of four apples, showing a total of twelve apples.

labels.description: Four apples in the first basket.
Four apples in the second basket.
Four apples in the third basket.

annotations.steps: Count three groups of four apples each to set up repeated addition.
annotations.strategy: I notice that putting equal groups together lets me add the same number multiple times instead of counting one by one.
annotations.misconceptions: A common error is counting the baskets themselves as the total instead of the apples inside them.
annotations.connections: Equal groups form the foundation for multiplication and division facts.
annotations.narrative: Add the $4$ apples across the $3$ baskets using repeated addition: $4 + 4 + 4 = 12$.

annotations.steps: Multiply the number of baskets by the apples in each basket.
annotations.strategy: I use multiplication instead of adding three fours.
annotations.misconceptions: Confusing multiplication with addition by adding the numbers instead of multiplying.
annotations.connections: Connects repeated addition to fast multiplication facts.
annotations.narrative: Multiply $3$ baskets by $4$ apples each to get $3 \times 4 = 12$, so Maya has $12$ apples in total.

specs.title: Model baskets with equal groups
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Understand total quantity conceptually by visualizing repeated addition as equal groups of items.
specs.seedNotes: Display 3 counted groups of 4 apples illustrating the repeated addition 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

specs.title: Multiply number of groups
specs.pedagogicalGoal: Transition from repeated addition to a concise multiplication expression for equal-sized groups.
specs.seedNotes: Write and evaluate the product of 3 baskets and 4 apples as 3 \times 4 = 12.

assignment.prompt: When you multiply the 3 baskets by the 4 apples in each basket ($3 \times 4$), what is the total number of apples?
assignment.rationale: Multiplying 3 groups of 4 apples gives 12 apples in total ($4 + 4 + 4 = 12$), whereas adding $3 + 4 = 7$ confuses multiplication with addition.
